verses.text: Abraham was old, and well stricken in age. Yahweh had blessed Abraham in all things.
Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, who ruled over all that he had, “Please put your hand under my thigh.
I will make you swear by Yahweh, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that you shall not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I live.
But you shall go to my country, and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son Isaac.”
The servant said to him, “What if the woman isn’t willing to follow me to this land? Must I bring your son again to the land you came from?”
Abraham said to him, “Beware that you don’t bring my son there again.

Yahweh, the God of heaven, who took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my birth, who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying, ‘I will give this land to your offspring.  He will send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
If the woman isn’t willing to follow you, then you shall be clear from this oath to me. Only you shall not bring my son there again.”
The servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and swore to him concerning this matter.
The servant took ten camels, of his master’s camels, and departed, having a variety of good things of his master’s with him. He arose, and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
He made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water at the time of evening, the time that women go out to draw water.
He said, “Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, please give me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
Behold, I am standing by the spring of water. The daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

Let it happen, that the young lady to whom I will say, ‘Please let down your pitcher, that I may drink,’ and she will say, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink,’ — let her be the one you have appointed for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown kindness to my master.”
Before he had finished speaking, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher on her shoulder.
The young lady was very beautiful to look at, a virgin. No man had known her. She went down to the spring, filled her pitcher, and came up.
The servant ran to meet her, and said, “Please give me a drink, a little water from your pitcher.”
She said, “Drink, my lord.” She hurried, and let down her pitcher on her hand, and gave him drink.
When she had done giving him drink, she said, “I will also draw for your camels, until they have done drinking.”
She hurried, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again to the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.
The man looked steadfastly at her, remaining silent, to know whether Yahweh had made his journey prosperous or not.
As the camels had done drinking, the man took a golden ring of half a shekel  weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold,
and said, “Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father’s house for us to lodge in?”
She said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.”
She said moreover to him, “We have both straw and feed enough, and room to lodge in.”
The man bowed his head, and worshiped Yahweh.

He said, “Blessed be Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his loving kindness and his truth toward my master. As for me, Yahweh has led me on the way to the house of my master’s relatives.”
The young lady ran, and told her mother’s house about these words.
Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.

When he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, “This is what the man said to me,” he came to the man. Behold, he was standing by the camels at the spring.
He said, “Come in, you blessed of Yahweh. Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.”
The man came into the house, and he unloaded the camels. He gave straw and feed for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
Food was set before him to eat, but he said, “I will not eat until I have told my message.” He said, “Speak on.”
He said, “I am Abraham’s servant.
Yahweh has blessed my master greatly. He has become great. He has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male servants and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
Sarah, my master’s wife, bore a son to my master when she was old. He has given all that he has to him.
My master made me swear, saying, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live,
but you shall go to my father’s house, and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son.’
I asked my master, ‘What if the woman will not follow me?’
He said to me, ‘Yahweh, before whom I walk, will send his angel with you, and prosper your way. You shall take a wife for my son from my relatives, and of my father’s house.
Then will you be clear from my oath, when you come to my relatives. If they don’t give her to you, you shall be clear from my oath.’
I came today to the spring, and said, ‘Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, if now you do prosper my way which I go —
behold, I am standing by this spring of water. Let it happen, that the maiden who comes out to draw, to whom I will say, “Please give me a little water from your pitcher to drink,”
and she will tell me, “Drink, and I will also draw for your camels,” — let her be the woman whom Yahweh has appointed for my master’s son.’
Before I had finished speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came out with her pitcher on her shoulder. She went down to the spring, and drew. I said to her, ‘Please let me drink.’
She hurried and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink.’ So I drank, and she also gave the camels a drink.
I asked her, and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bore to him.’ I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her hands.
I bowed my head, and worshiped Yahweh, and blessed Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the right way to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.
Now if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me. If not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.”
Then Laban and Bethuel answered, “The thing proceeds from Yahweh. We can’t speak to you bad or good.
Behold, Rebekah is before you. Take her, and go, and let her be your master’s son’s wife, as Yahweh has spoken.”
When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed himself down to the earth to Yahweh.
The servant brought out jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious things to her brother and her mother.
They ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and stayed all night. They rose up in the morning, and he said, “Send me away to my master.”
Her brother and her mother said, “Let the young lady stay with us a few days, at least ten. After that she will go.”
He said to them, “Don’t hinder me, since Yahweh has prospered my way. Send me away that I may go to my master.”
They said, “We will call the young lady, and ask her.”
They called Rebekah, and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” She said, “I will go.”
They sent away Rebekah, their sister, with her nurse, Abraham’s servant, and his men.
They blessed Rebekah, and said to her, “Our sister, may you be the mother of thousands of ten thousands, and let your offspring  possess the gate of those who hate them.”
Rebekah arose with her ladies. They rode on the camels, and followed the man. The servant took Rebekah, and went his way.
Isaac came from the way of Beer Lahai Roi, for he lived in the land of the South.
Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the evening. He lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, there were camels coming.
Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she dismounted from the camel.
She said to the servant, “Who is the man who is walking in the field to meet us?” The servant said, “It is my master.” She took her veil, and covered herself.
The servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.
Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife. He loved her. Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.

footnotes.content: I see an old man who has learned the secret: Yahweh does bless. Not just with flocks and silver, but in all things. After so many long years, Abraham could look back and say so with gratitude. That kind of settled trust only comes from walking with the Lord a good long while.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An oath sealed under the thigh speaks of weighty trust. Abraham isn't making a casual request; he's entrusting his most precious hope - his son and the promise - to this faithful servant. I wonder if we ever pause to realize how much care goes into protecting the things the Lord has given us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham calls Yahweh by name - God of heaven and earth. How good it is to remember who holds the promise. He won't entrust Isaac's future to the gods of Canaan, but to the God who called him out. Our children's future is safest when it's bound to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land of promise is still ahead for Isaac in a sense; Abraham won't go back to it for a bride. He wants a wife from the family God used to preserve the line of promise. Sometimes faith looks forward, even when tempted to look back.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A practical question from a careful servant. He loves his master enough to think through the what-ifs. I appreciate that kind of faithful prudence. Yet even the wisest servant knows some questions must be left to the God who called.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham draws a firm line - Isaac must not return to Ur. The promise God gave to Abraham must remain with Isaac in the land of promise. Our faith isn't about going back to old places of security, but trusting God to keep us where He has put us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham speaks of Yahweh's angel going before. This isn't just good luck - it's covenant faith. The God who spoke and swore will also send help. I rest in the truth that before I take a step of obedience, the God who keeps His covenant has already gone before me.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham is careful to release the servant from the oath if the woman refuses. Faith doesn't force God's providence; it trusts Him. The servant is bound to obedience, but not to coercion. That balance of faithfulness and freedom is wise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The oath is taken in the old way, with hand under thigh. This is no trivial promise - it's made before Yahweh, the God of heaven and earth. I want my yes to mean yes, sealed by trust in the God who hears every promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant loads up ten camels with the best of Abraham's goods. He's not coming empty-handed to ask for a bride. There's generosity here - Abraham gives freely for the son he loves. How much more does our Father give generously for His Son, Jesus, to bring us home to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Evening at the well - the hour when women come to draw water. The servant arrives at just the right time, though he doesn't know it yet. Our God is faithful to order the smallest details for the keeping of His promises.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What a prayer! The servant doesn't pray for what he wants, but for success in the matter of his master. He asks for kindness shown to Abraham. I learn to pray not just for myself, but for the faithfulness and kindness of God toward those I love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He stands by the spring of water, waiting. Faithful obedience brings us to the place of prayer, but it also brings us to the place of waiting. The servant does both - he goes, and he prays, and he waits.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A specific, humble sign. The servant asks for kindness not just to him, but shown through a young woman willing to go the extra mile for a stranger and his camels. True godly character often shows up in small acts of generous service.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before he finished speaking. Oh, how faithful is our God to answer! The prayer is barely off his lips and Rebekah appears. The Lord delights to go before His servants and meet them in answered prayer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Beautiful in appearance and a virgin - outward grace and inward purity. God is preparing a suitable bride for Isaac. Our Lord Jesus is also preparing a bride for Himself, holy and without blemish, made so by His own grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant runs to meet her. After all this journey, his heart is eager to see if Yahweh has answered. I understand that longing - to know if the God who promised is faithful to do what He said.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She hurries to serve. 'Drink, my lord' - kind, respectful, and ready. Rebekah's heart is revealed in her haste to help. The Lord often uses willing hearts to accomplish the purposes of His covenant love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She doesn't just meet the request - she goes beyond it. Water for a stranger is one thing; drawing for ten thirsty camels is a lot of work. Grace-filled service gives more than required.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She hurries again and again. No grumbling, no counting the cost out loud. This young woman shows us what it looks like to have a heart of generosity. I pray the Lord would give me a servant's heart like hers.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant watches in silence, holding his breath to see. He knows this could be the answer. Faithful prayer often leads to silent wonder as we watch God work. He wants to know if Yahweh has made his journey prosperous.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When he's sure it's of the Lord, he gives gifts - a nose ring and bracelets of gold. These are not bribes, but tokens of gratitude and commitment. The God who provides has stirred this servant to give in return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now he asks the family questions. Providence opens the door, and godly wisdom walks through it. The servant is careful - he wants to know the way is clear to bring Rebekah to Isaac.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rebekah identifies herself clearly - daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah and Nahor, Abraham's brother. The family ties are exactly as God ordained. The God who keeps covenant leads us right to our relatives in His time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She offers straw, feed, and room to lodge. Hospitality runs deep in this family. The same generous heart that drew water now opens her home. Kindness begets kindness in those who fear the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant bows his head and worships Yahweh. No pride, no taking credit - just humble worship. When God answers, the only right response is to bow before Him and give Him all the glory.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He blesses Yahweh for lovingkindness and truth toward Abraham. Notice he doesn't thank Rebekah first - he thanks God first. The Lord has led him step by step to the house of his master's relatives. I want that same habit of seeing God's hand in answered prayer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rebekah runs home to tell her mother's house. News of God's faithfulness spreads quickly when shared. Good news is meant to be shared with those we love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Enter Laban - Rebekah's brother. He'll play a larger role later, but here he sees the gifts and hears the report. A heart that fears the Lord will run to see what God is doing; a covetous heart will see opportunity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Laban sees the ring and bracelets, hears Rebekah's words, and runs to the man at the spring. The gifts catch his eye first. It makes me pray that I would be more captivated by the God who gives than by the gifts He gives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Come in, you blessed of Yahweh.' Laban recognizes the hand of God, at least in words. May our homes be places where we welcome those whom the Lord has blessed and led.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant is cared for - camels unloaded, fed, feet washed. Hospitality in the ancient East was a sacred duty. How beautiful when God's people extend rest to weary servants doing God's work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Food is set before him, but he won't eat until he tells his message. This man has one priority - he must be faithful to deliver Abraham's commission. I want that same single-mindedness about the things the Lord has entrusted to me.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'I am Abraham's servant.' He doesn't introduce himself by name, but by whose he is. That's a lesson for us - our greatest identity is not who we are, but whose we are. First and foremost, we belong to the God of Abraham.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant gives glory to Yahweh for blessing Abraham. He recounts all the Lord has done - flocks, herds, silver, gold, servants, camels, donkeys. A grateful heart always traces blessings back to the faithful God who gives them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He points to Isaac as the heir of the promise - Sarah bore him in her old age, and Abraham has given him all that he has. Everything points to God's faithfulness to keep His word to give an heir through whom the promise would come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant faithfully repeats the oath and the charge. He doesn't embellish; he just tells what he was told. Faithful witnesses simply repeat what the Master has said.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham insisted on going to his own relatives for Isaac's bride. The line of promise was to be preserved within the family through whom God had revealed Himself. God cares about the spiritual heritage of those He calls.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant humbly recounts his doubt. He doesn't hide his questions from the family; he tells them honestly. Faithfulness includes honest prayer even when our hearts wonder how God will do it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham says, 'Yahweh, before whom I walk.' What a testimony! A life of walking with God gives confidence to others. The God who walks with His people also sends His angel to prosper the way of obedience.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant carefully explains the conditions of release from the oath. He's not trying to manipulate, just to be faithful and clear. Integrity in covenant matters - even in matters of marriage.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now the servant tells how he prayed at the very spring where they sit. He's recounting God's faithfulness step by step. Our testimonies of answered prayer strengthen faith in others.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He repeats his simple sign to them. He asked for nothing extraordinary - just a heart of kindness toward a stranger. The Lord often answers the simplest prayers of faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant wanted the one whom Yahweh had appointed. That's the heart of faith - not just 'is this good?', but 'is this of the Lord?' We need that same discernment in the big decisions of life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before he finished speaking in his heart - again, God answered before the prayer was complete. The Lord knows our needs and answers in His perfect timing, often exceeding what we dared to ask.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rebekah's response matches the sign exactly - down to the details. God's providence is precise. He doesn't just point generally; He leads us by specific, faithful steps.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant gives gifts and confirms the family connection. He moves from prayer to worship. The ring on her nose and bracelets on her hands mark her as belonging to the house of Abraham - soon to be Isaac's bride.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He bows and worships, blessing Yahweh for leading him in the right way. The servant never took credit for finding Rebekah - he gave God all the glory. That should be our habit too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now he leaves the decision in their hands. Faithful service presents the matter clearly and respectfully, then lets others respond. He'll go either way as the Lord directs - a posture of humble trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Laban and Bethuel see it clearly - 'The thing proceeds from Yahweh.' When God is at work, even those outside Abraham's household can recognize His hand. May our lives be so marked by God's faithfulness that others see it too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rebekah is before them - take her and go. The decision is made. God's timing is perfect. What was prayed for in faith is now given in faithfulness by those who fear Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hearing the answer, the servant bows himself down to the earth to Yahweh. More worship. Another prayer answered brings another act of adoration. God is worthy of praise for every act of faithfulness to His promises.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant brings out treasures and gives them to Rebekah, and also to her brother and mother. Abraham's blessing flows to others. God's covenant love is generous and overflows to those connected to it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They eat, drink, and stay the night. A time of fellowship after God has done a great thing. Then the servant is eager to go - he wants to return to his master with the good news. Faithful servants long to complete their task.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Her family wants a few more days with Rebekah. That's natural and loving. Parting is sweet sorrow. Even when God is leading, there can be tears in leaving those we love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Don't hinder me, since Yahweh has prospered my way.' The servant is gentle but firm. When God has clearly opened the door, we shouldn't delay obedience out of sentiment. There is a time to go.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They wisely ask Rebekah herself. In matters that affect her life, her voice matters. Godly families give room for others to discern and obey the Lord for themselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'I will go.' What faith! Rebekah leaves her home, her family, her country to go to a land she's never seen, to marry a man she's never met. All because she trusts that Yahweh is leading. May I have that kind of trust in my God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They send her away with her nurse and with Abraham's servant and his men. She's well cared for for the journey. God provides companions and protection for those who obey Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A beautiful blessing - 'Our sister, may you be the mother of thousands of ten thousands, and let your offspring possess the gate of those who hate them.' This echoes God's promise to Abraham. God is extending His covenant blessing through Isaac and Rebekah to bless all families of the earth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rebekah arises with her ladies and rides the camels to follow the man. She goes willingly, with joy and purpose. The bride of Isaac sets off to meet her bridegroom - a picture that points me to the church hastening to meet our Bridegroom, Jesus Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Isaac comes from Beer Lahai Roi - the place where Hagar met the God who sees. Isaac has been dwelling in the South, meditating and waiting. The God who sees is bringing the answer to his prayers too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Isaac goes out to meditate in the field at evening. A man of prayer, communing with his God as the day ends. I love that the Lord brings his bride to him while he's in prayer. How often God answers while we're talking to Him!
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rebekah lifts up her eyes and sees Isaac. She dismounts from the camel. There's excitement and reverence both. Soon she will become his wife, and a new chapter of God's faithfulness begins.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Who is the man...?' 'It is my master.' She takes her veil and covers herself - a sign of modesty and readiness for marriage. There's a beautiful humility here as she prepares to meet her bridegroom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The servant tells Isaac all the things that he had done. He gives a full account of God's faithfulness. Faithful servants don't just do the work - they report back with thanksgiving for all the Lord has done.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Looking back across the years, I see how God brings His bride to His Son. Isaac brought Rebekah into Sarah's tent and loved her; our Jesus brings His church into the joy of His Father's house and loves us with an everlasting love. As of 2026-10, I'm grateful that the God who arranged this long ago is still bringing His people home to His Son.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
